name: Newton's Second Law Application
description: Applying F = ma to analyze forces and acceleration in a system. Identify all forces, set up coordinate system, and write net force equations.
recognition_cues: Multiple forces acting on an object
Asked to find acceleration or force
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to include all forces (especially normal force or friction)
Wrong sign convention for forces
Confusing mass with weight
Not breaking forces into components on inclined planes

name: Free Body Diagram Construction
description: Drawing all forces acting on an isolated body. Essential first step for any force analysis problem.
recognition_cues: Object connected by ropes, springs, or cables
Need to analyze forces on a specific object
common_pitfalls: Drawing forces on the wrong object
Missing the normal force from contact surfaces
Including internal forces in the FBD
Forgetting tension in attached strings/ropes

name: Newton's Third Law Pairs
description: Identifying action-reaction force pairs that are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, acting on different bodies.
recognition_cues: Asked about force on one object due to another
common_pitfalls: Confusing 3rd law pairs with balanced forces on same object
Thinking 3rd law pairs cancel each other
Not recognizing that pairs act on DIFFERENT bodies
Confusing normal force and weight as a 3rd law pair

name: Friction Force Analysis
description: Analyzing static and kinetic friction forces. Understanding μN relationship and when each type applies.
recognition_cues: Object sliding or about to slide
Question about minimum force to move object
common_pitfalls: Using kinetic friction when object is stationary
Forgetting that static friction has a maximum value
Using wrong normal force (especially on inclines)
Not recognizing that friction opposes relative motion

name: Inclined Plane Analysis
description: Analyzing motion on inclined surfaces. Decomposing weight into parallel and perpendicular components.
recognition_cues: Object on a slope or ramp
Asked about acceleration down a ramp
common_pitfalls: Using wrong trig function (sin vs cos)
Not tilting coordinate system with the incline
Forgetting normal force equals mg·cos(θ), not mg
Wrong direction for friction force

name: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
description: Applying energy conservation when no non-conservative forces do work. KE + PE = constant.
recognition_cues: No friction or friction explicitly negligible
common_pitfalls: Using energy conservation when friction is present
Wrong reference point for potential energy
Forgetting spring potential energy
Not recognizing when work-energy theorem is better

name: Work-Energy Theorem
description: Net work equals change in kinetic energy. Useful when non-conservative forces are present.
recognition_cues: Asked for final speed or distance traveled
common_pitfalls: Not including work by all forces
Using wrong angle in W = F·d·cos(θ)
Confusing work done by vs work done on
Forgetting friction always does negative work on moving object

name: Conservation of Momentum
description: Total momentum is conserved in collisions when no external forces act. p_initial = p_final.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting momentum is a vector
Wrong signs for velocity directions
Confusing elastic vs inelastic collisions
Not recognizing 2D momentum conservation needs two equations

name: Uniform Circular Motion
description: Object moving in a circle at constant speed. Centripetal acceleration = v²/r directed toward center.
recognition_cues: Radius and speed or period given
Asked about centripetal force or acceleration
Banked curves, orbits, or spinning objects
common_pitfalls: Treating centripetal force as a separate force
Confusing centripetal and centrifugal
Using wrong direction for acceleration
Forgetting to identify what provides the centripetal force

name: Spring Force and Energy
description: Hooke's Law (F = -kx) and spring potential energy (U = ½kx²). Analyzing oscillating systems.
common_pitfalls: Using wrong sign for restoring force
Confusing x = 0 with natural length vs equilibrium
Forgetting to square displacement in PE formula
Not recognizing spring force is position-dependent

name: Coulomb's Law
description: Calculating electric force between point charges. F = kq₁q₂/r². Force is attractive for opposite charges, repulsive for like charges.
recognition_cues: Two or more point charges given
Charges given in Coulombs or microcoulombs
common_pitfalls: Forgetting force is a vector - need direction
Using diameter instead of center-to-center distance
Wrong sign interpretation (force direction vs charge sign)
Not using correct value of k (9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)

name: Electric Field
description: Electric field E = F/q = kQ/r² for point charges. Field points away from positive charges, toward negative charges.
recognition_cues: Asked about electric field strength or direction
Point charge or charge distribution given
Field lines or field vectors discussed
common_pitfalls: Confusing field direction with force direction on negative charges
Forgetting to find vector sum for multiple charges
Using wrong formula for non-point charge distributions
Not recognizing when to use Gauss's Law instead

name: Superposition Principle (E&M)
description: Net electric field or force is the vector sum of individual contributions. Apply separately then add as vectors.
recognition_cues: Asked for net field or force at a point
Need to find where field is zero
common_pitfalls: Adding magnitudes instead of vectors
Forgetting to break into components
Wrong direction for individual field contributions
Not recognizing symmetry that cancels components

name: Gauss's Law
description: Φ = ∮E·dA = Q_enclosed/ε₀. Use symmetric Gaussian surfaces to find electric fields efficiently.
recognition_cues: High symmetry: spherical, cylindrical, or planar
common_pitfalls: Choosing wrong Gaussian surface shape
Including charge outside the Gaussian surface
Forgetting E is constant on the surface by symmetry
Not recognizing when Gauss's Law is easier than direct integration

name: Electric Potential and Voltage
description: V = kQ/r for point charges. Potential is scalar (no direction). Work W = qΔV. Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to field lines.
common_pitfalls: Confusing potential (scalar) with field (vector)
Wrong sign for work done by/against electric force
Forgetting potential is relative (need reference point)
Confusing V (potential) with U (potential energy)

name: Capacitors and Capacitance
description: C = Q/V. Energy stored U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C. Series and parallel combinations.
common_pitfalls: Confusing series/parallel formulas (opposite of resistors)
Forgetting what stays constant when dielectric inserted
Not recognizing isolated vs connected to battery
Wrong area or separation in parallel plate formula

name: Ohm's Law and Resistance
description: V = IR. Resistance R = ρL/A. Power P = IV = I²R = V²/R. Resistors in series and parallel.
common_pitfalls: Using wrong formula for series vs parallel resistors
Confusing current through vs voltage across
Forgetting units (especially for resistivity)
Not recognizing when Ohm's Law doesn't apply

name: Kirchhoff's Laws
description: Junction rule: ΣI_in = ΣI_out. Loop rule: ΣV = 0 around any closed loop. Essential for complex circuits.
common_pitfalls: Inconsistent sign convention for voltage drops
Wrong current direction assumption (answer will be negative)
Missing a loop equation
Not using enough independent equations

name: Magnetic Force on Moving Charges
description: F = qv×B. Force is perpendicular to both velocity and field. Use right-hand rule. Causes circular motion.
recognition_cues: Charged particle moving in magnetic field
common_pitfalls: Forgetting force is perpendicular to velocity (no work done)
Wrong hand rule for negative charges
Confusing magnetic force with electric force
Not recognizing when particle moves parallel to B (no force)

name: Magnetic Force on Current-Carrying Wires
description: F = IL×B. Force on wire segment in magnetic field. Basis for electric motors.
recognition_cues: Wire carrying current in magnetic field
Length of wire in field given
Force on wire or torque on loop
common_pitfalls: Using total wire length instead of length in field
Wrong direction from right-hand rule
Forgetting force is zero when wire parallel to B
Not treating current direction as a vector

name: Magnetic Field from Currents
description: Biot-Savart law for field from current element. B = μ₀I/2πr for infinite wire. B = μ₀I/2R at center of loop.
recognition_cues: Specific geometries: straight wire, loop, solenoid
common_pitfalls: Using wrong formula for geometry
Forgetting field direction from right-hand rule
Wrong distance in formula
Not recognizing when to use Ampere's Law instead

name: Electromagnetic Induction (Faraday's Law)
description: EMF = -dΦ/dt. Changing magnetic flux induces voltage. Lenz's law: induced current opposes change.
recognition_cues: Coil or loop with changing area
common_pitfalls: Forgetting the negative sign (Lenz's law)
Wrong flux calculation (Φ = BA cos θ)
Not identifying what's changing (B, A, or θ)
Confusing motional EMF with transformer EMF

name: Inductors and Inductance
description: Self-inductance L, EMF = -L(dI/dt). Energy stored U = ½LI². RL circuit time constant τ = L/R.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting inductor opposes current CHANGE, not current
Wrong time constant formula (τ = L/R, not RC)
Not recognizing inductor acts like wire at steady state
Sign errors with induced EMF
